reporting-org.narrative: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

description.narrative: Provision of long-term senior secured loan of up to USD 33 million (EUR 30 million equivalent) tranche to Red Sea Wind Energy to finance the construction of a 150 MW extension of a 500 MW wind power plant currently under construction in the Gulf of Suez, approximately 40km North-West of Ras Ghareb in Egypt. The extension will increase the total capacity of the plant to 650 MW. This comes in addition to a long-term senior secured loan of up to USD 100 million (EUR 96 million equivalent) in total signed in March 2023, comprising of a portion of up to USD 50 million (EUR 46 million equivalent) for the Bank's account, and up to USD 50 million (EUR 46 million equivalent) for the account of the Green Climate Fund to finance the construction of the initial 500 MW. Once operational, the Project will be one of the largest privately developed utility scale wind power plants in Egypt and will support the country in increasing its renewable energy capacity. Through delivery of clean power at one of the most competitive wind tariffs in the country and wider region, the Project will support Egypt's renewable transition and exploitation of the exceptional wind resources in the Gulf of Suez area. The Project is expected to further improve the environmental characteristics of Egypt's power sector by reducing emissions of local pollutants and CO2, as well as water consumption.
